content: 1. C et al. conducted an antigen-specific evaluation of the immunological status of various groups in a leprosy-endemic region, as published in BMC Infectious Diseases in 2015. 2. Wang H, Liu W, Jin Y, Yu M, Jiang H, Tamura T, and colleagues identified antibodies to Mycobacterium leprae PGL-I and MMP-II as potential markers for early-stage leprosy diagnosis, as reported in Diagnostic Microbiology and Infectious Disease in 2015. 3. Da Silva CR, Lyon S, Araos R, Lyon AC, de Faria Grossi MA, Lyon SE, and others analyzed the patterns of ML Flow and ELISA (PGL-I) serological tests in leprosy-endemic and non-endemic areas, as published in Revista da Sociedade Brasileira de Medicina Tropical in 2008. 4. Tsukamoto Y, Maeda Y, and Makino M evaluated the utility of major membrane protein-I (MMP-I) as a serodiagnostic tool for paucibacillary leprosy, as detailed in Diagnostic Microbiology and Infectious Disease in 2014. 5. Duthie MS, Raychaudhuri R, Tutterrow YL, Misquith A, Bowman J, Casey A, and colleagues developed a rapid ELISA for diagnosing multibacillary leprosy by detecting antibodies against a novel protein-glycolipid conjugate, as published in Diagnostic Microbiology and Infectious Disease in 2014. 6. Duthie MS, Orcullo FM, Abbelana J, Maghanoy A, Balagon MF, and others conducted a comparative evaluation of antibody detection tests to aid in diagnosing multibacillary leprosy, as reported in Applied Microbiology and Biotechnology in 2016. 7. Stefani MM, Grassi AB, Sampaio LH, Sousa AL, Costa MB, Scheelbeek P, and colleagues compared two rapid tests for anti-phenolic glycolipid-I serology in Brazil and Nepal, as published in Memórias do Instituto Oswaldo Cruz in 2012. 8. Penna ML, Penna GO, Iglesias PC, Natal S, Rodrigues LC performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to assess anti-PGL-I positivity as a risk marker for leprosy development among contacts of leprosy cases, as reported in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases in 2016. 9. Rudeeaneksin J, Srisungngam S, Sawanpanyalert P, Sittiwakin T, Likanonsakul S, Pasadorn S, and others developed a LightCycler real-time PCR method for rapid detection and quantification of Mycobacterium leprae in skin specimens, as published in FEMS Immunology and Medical Microbiology in 2008. 10. Bang PD, Suzuki K, Phuong le T, Chu TM, Ishii N, Khang TH evaluated PCR-based detection of Mycobacterium leprae for leprosy diagnosis, as detailed in the Journal of Dermatology in 2009. 11. Martinez AN, Ribeiro-Alves M, Sarno EN, Moraes MO assessed qPCR-based assays for leprosy diagnosis directly in clinical specimens, as published in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases in 2011. 12. Caleffi KR, Hirata RD, Hirata MH, Caleffi ER, Siqueira VL, Cardoso RF utilized polymerase chain reaction (PCR) to detect Mycobacterium leprae in urine, as reported in the Brazilian Journal of Medical and Biological Research in 2012. 13. Wen Y, Xing Y, Yuan LC, Liu J, Zhang Y, Li HY developed a whole-blood nested-PCR amplification method for early diagnosis of leprosy by detecting M. leprae-specific DNA, as published in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2013. 14. Banerjee S, Biswas N, Kanti Das N, Sil A, Ghosh P, Hasanoor Raja AH, and others revisited the role of slit-skin smear and critically analyzed the applicability of PCR in leprosy diagnosis, as reported in the International Journal of Dermatology in 2011. 15. Silva AR, Queiroz MFA, Ishikawa AYE, Silvestre MPSA, Xavier MB evaluated the agreement between different diagnostic tests for leprosy, as published in the Journal Brasileiro de Patologia e Medicina Laboratorial in 2017. 16. Jain S, Visser LH, Praveen TL, Rao PN, Surekha T, Ellanti R, and others introduced high-resolution sonography as a novel technique to detect nerve damage in leprosy, as reported in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases in 2009. 17. Elias J Jr, Nogueira-Barbosa MH, Feltrin LT, Furini RB, Foss NT, Marques W Jr, and colleagues explored the role of ulnar nerve sonography in leprosy neuropathy with electrophysiologic correlation, as published in the Journal of Ultrasound in Medicine in 2009. 18. Bathala L, Kumar K, Pathapati R, Jain S, Visser LH studied ulnar neuropathy in Hansen's disease using clinical, high-resolution ultrasound, and electrophysiological correlations, as reported in the Journal of Clinical Neurophysiology in 2012. 19. Bathala L, Kumar P, Kumar K, Visser LH established normal ultrasonographic cross-sectional area values of the ulnar nerve along its course in the arm with electrophysiological correlations in 100 Asian subjects, as published in Muscle & Nerve in 2013. 20. Frade MA, Nogueira-Barbosa MH, Lugão HB, Furini RB, Marques Júnior W, Foss NT introduced new sonographic measures of peripheral nerves as a diagnostic tool for peripheral nerve involvement in leprosy, as published in Memórias do Instituto Oswaldo Cruz in 2013. 21. Lugão HB, Nogueira-Barbosa MH, Marques Jr W, Foss NT, Frade MAC demonstrated asymmetric nerve enlargement as a characteristic of leprosy neuropathy using ultrasonography, as reported in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases. 22. Gupta S, Bhatt S, Bhargava SK, Singal A, Bhargava S utilized high-resolution sonographic examination as a new technique to study ulnar nerve neuropathy in leprosy, as published in Leprosy Review in 2016. 23. Lugão HB, Frade MA, Marques W Jr, Foss NT, Nogueira-Barbosa MH conducted a longitudinal prospective study on ultrasonography of leprosy neuropathy, as reported in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases in 2016. 24. Bathala L, Kumar P, Kumar K, Shaik A, Visser LH established normal values of the median nerve cross-sectional area obtained by ultrasound along its course in the arm with electrophysiological correlations in 100 Asian subjects, as published in Muscle & Nerve in 2014. 25. Boehm J, Scheidl E, Bereczki D, Schelle T, Aranyi Z measured 14 nerve segments in 56 healthy subjects using high-resolution ultrasonography and assessed reliability, as published in Ultraschall in der Medizin in 2014.
